page_summary:
Schizophrenia and the Book of Changes is the canonical works-table record for PKD's primary text corpus item. The record links the archive's preserved manifestation of the work to the broader corpus and gives researchers a single place to follow its bibliographic and interpretive context.

The preserved archive item here is Schizophrenia and the Book of Changes (Unknown).

The source record itself summarizes the work as follows: A 22-page scanned document of Philip K. Dick's essay 'Schizophrenia and the Book of Changes,' a known non-fiction philosophical piece. No OCR text layer is present. In this essay, Dick explores the relationship between schizophrenic perception and the divinatory system of the I Ching (Book of Changes), the ancient Chinese oracle that played a significant role in his creative process.

Dick famously used the I Ching to plot The Man in the High Castle (1962), consulting the oracle to determine narrative decisions, and the Book of Changes appears as a central element within the novel itself. This essay represents Dick's theoretical engagement with the I Ching's implications for understanding consciousness, reality, and the nature of meaningful patterns. The connection between schizophrenia and the I Ching reflects Dick's lifelong interest in altered states of consciousness as potential modes of perceiving hidden structures of reality.

The entry is most useful when tracing publication context, later commentary, or relationships to other works.
